ever, there is some controversy regarding what constitutes

Vitamin-Mineral Supplements
Forty percent of preschool children are given a multivitamin-
mineral supplement; this percentage decreases in older children 
(Butte et al, 2010; Picciano et al, 2007). Families with more edu-
cation, health insurance coverage, and higher incomes generally 
have higher rates of supplement use, although these may not be 
the families who are at greatest risk for having inadequate diets.
Evidence shows that fluoride can help prevent dental caries. 
If a community’s water supply is not fluoridated, fluoride sup-
plements are recommended from 6 months until 16 years of 
age. However, individual family practices should be assessed, 
including the child’s primary source of fluids (e.g., drinking 
water, juices, or other beverages) and fluoride sources from 
child care, school, toothpaste, and mouthwash (see Chapter 25).
